item.title: Indonesia Bans Freight Trucks from Toll Roads Until Jan 4
item.description: Jakarta. Indonesia has imposed a nationwide ban on freight trucks using toll roads until January 4, 2026, as part of measures to ease traffic congestion and improve road safety during the Christmas and New Year holiday period. item.title: Bandung Land Sinking Faster Than 5 Centimeters Annually, Geology Agency Warns
item.description: Bandung. Land in the Greater Bandung area is sinking at a rate exceeding five centimeters per year, a trend that has also been recorded in several coastal cities across Java, Indonesia’s Badan Geologi said on Sunday. The phenomenon has drawn particular concern in Bandung, which sits in a highland basin, as land subsidence is more commonly associated with coastal regions. item.title: Optimizing Private Coal Hauling Road Operations, RMKE Carries Coal for 3 New Customers
item.description: Jakarta. PT RMK Energy Tbk (RMKE IJ), an integrated coal logistics service provider, continues to expand its customer base approaching the end of 2025. item.title: Indonesia Signs Trade Deal with Russia’s Eurasian Bloc Amid US Tariffs
item.description: Jakarta. Indonesia and the Russia-backed Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) have just signed a free trade pact, a document that is expected to act as a cushion against rising US protectionism. Trade Minister Budi Santoso represented Jakarta at the signing ceremony in St. Petersburg on Sunday local time. item.title: Gold Rally Continues, Antam Bullion Breaks Another Record to Rp 2.5 Mill
item.description: Jakarta. Gold prices in Indonesia climbed further on Monday, with Aneka Tambang (Antam) bullion rising Rp 11,000 to a fresh all-time high of Rp 2,502,000 ($149.29) per gram, extending the precious metal’s recent rally. Data from Logam Mulia showed that Antam gold had already set a previous record on Saturday after gaining Rp 8,000 to Rp 2,491,000 per gram. The latest increase pushed prices to a new peak. item.title: The Archipelago's New Oil: How Rare Earths Could Redefine Indonesia's Role in Global Power
item.description: Rare earth elements (REEs) are fast emerging as one of the world's most strategic commodities. REEs are a group of 17 chemically similar elements critical to key technologies such as renewables or electric vehicles. They are widely available, but rarely found in concentrated deposits, which makes their extraction and processing costly and technically challenging. item.title: Indonesia Bond Market Outlook Brightens in 2026 on Global Rate Cuts
item.description: Jakarta. Indonesia’s government bond (SBN) and corporate bond markets are expected to maintain a positive outlook in 2026, supported by a continued global monetary easing cycle amid expectations of interest rate cuts by the Federal Reserve and other major central banks. Declining global interest rates have pushed yields lower in developed markets, prompting global investors to seek higher returns in emerging markets, including Indonesia, according to Pefindo Fixed Income Analyst Ahmad Nasrudin.

item.title: Bank Indonesia Rebukes Cash Refusal After Elderly Woman Denied Bread Purchase
item.description: Jakarta. The central bank has issued a firm response after a viral social media video showed an elderly woman being denied the purchase of bread at a Roti’O outlet for attempting to pay in cash. Bank Indonesia said the rupiah is legal tender across the country and must not be refused in payment transactions. item.title: Indonesia Repatriates Bodies of 9 Citizens Killed in Hong Kong Apartment Fire
item.description: Jakarta. Indonesia has begun the repatriation process for the bodies of nine citizens who had died in the catastrophic Hong Kong high-rise fire. In late November, a blaze engulfed Hong Kong’s Wang Fuk Court apartment complex and claimed 160 lives, 9 of whom were Indonesians. The Indonesian government recently said that they had kept in touch with their families early this month for both the paperwork and the victims’ paychecks.
